close_reason: Migrated DeviationScope::issuer_dn_exact and ::serial_range from &x509_cert::name::Name to impl Into<Vec<u8>>; both return Self directly (no Result, no encode step). OSCAL parse side drops the parse-and-re-encode round-trip — keeps decode_name as a typed-error guard but flows the raw DER bytes through to the constructor. All call sites updated (tests in deviation.rs, oscal::emit, oscal::parse). x509-cert is no longer named in either constructor's signature; the remaining der::Error leak in oscal::parse::ParseError is tracked separately under PKIX-7f92.31. No external callers exist; migration is workspace-local. 286 pkix-lint tests pass; workspace builds clean. Commit cac8a353.
description:
pkix-lint/src/deviation.rs:512 and :534 — Both DeviationScope constructors take &x509_cert::name::Name:

  pub fn issuer_dn_exact(name: &x509_cert::name::Name) -> Result<Self, der::Error>
  pub fn serial_range(issuer: &x509_cert::name::Name, start: Vec<u8>, end: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Self, der::Error>

Internally, both constructors immediately encode the Name to DER bytes via name.to_der() for storage in the props bag. The typed parameter is gratuitous — pkix-lint stores and compares raw DER bytes (see prop_issuer_dn_der / serial_cmp).

CALLER IMPACT: pinning x509-cert's pre-1.0 major version (currently 0.3.x, with active development toward 1.0) directly into pkix-lint's public API. When x509-cert cuts 1.0 — or just changes Name's internal shape in a 0.x.y bump — these two constructors break.

A caller that has DER bytes (the common case in pkix-lint's intended workflow — deviations are policy entries authored by operators from observed cert data, not from in-flight Certificate structs) is forced to:
  let name: Name = Name::from_der(&issuer_der)?;
  let scope = DeviationScope::issuer_dn_exact(&name)?;  // encodes back to DER

That is an unnecessary parse-and-re-encode round-trip.

REMEDIATION: Change the parameter type to &[u8] (DER bytes):

  pub fn issuer_dn_exact(issuer_der: &[u8]) -> Result<Self, DeviationScopeError>
  pub fn serial_range(issuer_der: &[u8], start: Vec<u8>, end: Vec<u8>) -> Result<Self, DeviationScopeError>

Document the DER encoding contract: "issuer_der is the DER encoding of the issuer Name (the value of TBSCertificate.issuer or Certificate.tbs_certificate.issuer.to_der()). The bytes are stored verbatim and compared byte-equal during matching."

Callers with a Name in hand call `name.to_der().unwrap()` at the call site — that's where they have x509-cert as a dep anyway.

This decouples pkix-lint's deviation-store API entirely from x509-cert's evolution. Combined with the der::Error wrapping fix (separate finding), DeviationScope's public surface stops depending on either upstream crate.

ALTERNATIVE: keep &Name but document the version-pin commitment in rustdoc. This is cheaper to implement but pins x509-cert forever.

Pre-1.0 free for the &[u8] migration.

Note: deviation.rs:494 (issuer_dn_contains) takes String / &str, which is fine. The two constructors flagged here are the only x509-cert leak in the DeviationScope public surface.
title: DeviationScope::issuer_dn_exact and ::serial_range take &x509_cert::name::Name; pins x509-cert pre-1.0 major version gratuitously (constructor immediately re-encodes to DER)
